questions.q: Describe how the graph of $g(x) = 2^{x-3} + 1$ is obtained from the graph of $y = 2^x$, and state the asymptote of $g$.
questions.answer: Shift right 3 units and up 1 unit. Horizontal asymptote: $y = 1$.

questions.q: The graph below passes through $(0, 1)$, $(1, 2)$, and $(2, 4)$. Write the equation of the exponential function shown.
An investment of 1000 riyals grows with continuous compounding at an annual rate of 6%: $A(t) = 1000e^{0.06t}$. Find the value after 5 years, to the nearest riyal.
Determine whether each function represents growth or decay:
2000 riyals is invested at 5% annual interest, compounded monthly, using $A = P\left(1+\frac{r}{n}\right)^{nt}$.
parts: Find the value after 3 years, to the nearest riyal.
Find the value after 3 years if compounded continuously instead ($A = Pe^{rt}$), to the nearest riyal.

questions.q: How much must be invested now at 4% annual interest compounded annually to have 10,000 riyals in 8 years? Round to the nearest riyal.
Two investments start at 500 riyals: one grows at 4% per year, the other at 7% per year. Find the value of each after 10 years, to the nearest riyal, and their difference.
Rank the following functions from slowest to fastest growth as $x \to \infty$: $y=x^{10}$, $y=2^x$, $y=1.01^x$.
questions.answer: Any exponential with base $>1$ eventually outgrows any polynomial, no matter how slowly it starts. So even though $1.01^x$ grows very slowly at first, it eventually overtakes $x^{10}$. Long-run ranking (slowest to fastest): $x^{10} < 1.01^x < 2^x$.
